chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was sitting in the circle of Rabi'ah al-Ra'y. An Arab came and asked Rabi'ah a question, and he answered him. When he fell silent, the Arab said to him, 'Is it in your neck?' Rabi'ah remained silent and did not reply to him. He repeated the question, and he answered him similarly. The Arab said to him, 'Is it in your neck?' Rabi'ah remained silent. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'It is in his neck.' He said, 'Did he not say,
Every jurist/mufti is liable (for his ruling).

key_terms.أَعْرَابِيٌّ: An Arab, often used in hadith to denote a person from the desert or a simple, direct questioner
key_terms.رَبِيعَةَ الرَّأْيِ: Rabi'ah al-Ra'y, a prominent early Shia jurist known for his independent reasoning
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: Liable, responsible, or guaranteeing the correctness of his ruling
key_terms.فِي عُنُقِهِ: In his neck, a metaphorical expression meaning he bears the responsibility or liability for the ruling
key_terms.مُفْتٍ: A jurist who issues fatwas (legal opinions)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'in his neck' in the context of Islamic jurisprudence and fatwa liability?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the concept of 'daman' (liability) for jurists, illustrating that Rabi'ah al-Ra'y’s silence confirmed his personal responsibility for the legal ruling he issued. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly links this to the prophetic principle that every mufti is a guarantor for his fatwa, emphasizing the weight of scholarly authority in Shia jurisprudence. This incident serves as a critical precedent for understanding the accountability of mujtahids in the school of thought.
